subject: Chemistry
chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
central_question: How do atomic number and electronic configuration generate repeating trends in elemental properties?
in_scope_units: Modern periodic law, groups, and periods.
s-, p-, d-, and f-block configurations.
Ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and electronegativity.
Valence, oxidation states, metallic character, and reactivity.

known_pitfalls.correction: He mainly used atomic mass and chemical similarity.

known_pitfalls.claim: Atomic radius increases across a period.
known_pitfalls.correction: It generally decreases as effective nuclear charge rises.

known_pitfalls.claim: Cations are larger than their atoms.
known_pitfalls.correction: Cations are generally smaller; anions are generally larger.

known_pitfalls.claim: Fluorine has the most negative electron gain enthalpy.
known_pitfalls.correction: Chlorine is more negative because fluorine has stronger small-shell repulsion.
One concerns bonded atoms; the other is an isolated-atom energy change.
